text:
alex: Heads-up — Enterprise POC with AcmeCorp just moved to commit stage. They want reserved GPUs + autoscale. Need a sizing plan and answers for their security QA (KMS/HSM, logs retention). Can we list throughput targets and preheat plan? PO#12345. @sarah FYI

sarah: Quick summary from the call: target ~6k requests/min peak, avg payload small (1–3 short assistant turns). SLA asks: p95 < 350ms for our chat path. Budget leaning to 4 dedicated GPUs but wants burst option. Need pricing delta for reserved vs on-demand.

mike: Quick notes — clarify requests vs tokens first. If that 6k is requests/min we can estimate. For a quantized medium model on A10X-class instance: ~120–160 tokens/sec per GPU (varies). Autoscale notes: prefer 4 reserved + 2 burst slots for safety. Recommend warmup and KV cache priming 10–15 min before peak.

liz: Proposed autoscale / warmup config (example):
```yaml
autoscale:
  min_replicas: 4
  max_replicas: 8
  target_gpu_util: 0.65
  scale_up_cooldown: 90s
  scale_down_cooldown: 300s
  scale_policy: "prefer_reserved_then_burst"
warmup:
  method: kv_prefix
  keys: "/acme/*"
  duration_s: 900
batching:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_size: 32
  max_latency_ms: 40
fallback:
  model_variant: gpt-medium-quantized-8bit
```
Notes: disable scale-down during critical windows. Enable prefix KV warmup using their most common session ids.

mike: Sizing math quick calc: if 6k req/min = 100 req/sec and avg response ~12 tokens => ~1200 tokens/sec total. 1 A10X at 120 tokens/sec -> ~10 GPUs naive. But batching reduces effective token cost: with 32 batch and short responses we pick up 3–4x efficiency. So 4 reserved + 2 burst is plausible with good batching and caching.

julia: Security checklist items from their questionnaire: KMS integration (customer-managed keys), option for HSM-based key storage (add-on), VPC peering or Private deployment, audit log retention window (we can commit to 365 days for Dedicated customers), and SOC2 attestation copy required. I can attach the SOC2 PDF and KMS integration guide to the ticket. HSM adds ~3–4% to infra cost.

sales-ops: Pricing note: we can offer a 6-month reserved commit for 4 GPUs and include 2 burst credits per month. Ballpark: ~20% discount vs on-demand per-token when reserved. Adding HSM + extended retention is billable. I'll prepare a formal quote.

alex: Can someone add a short runbook snippet for the POC so we can hand to the customer? Need: (1) load generator command, (2) warmup step, (3) failure mode and fallback.

liz: Runbook snippet below — paste into their ticket: 
```bash
# simple loadtest example (from customer VPC)
./loadtest --target https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \\n  --rps 100 --duration 1800 \\n  --payload '{"prompt":"warmup","tokens":8}'

# warmup step (server-side preheat)
redwoodctl preheat --project acme --prefix "/acme/*" --duration 900
```
Replace endpoint for dedicated VPC path.

mike: Failure modes to call out in runbook: cache-miss storm (many cold sessions at once) — mitigation: rate-limiter + degrade to smaller quantized variant + queue shed; provisioning lag for additional reserved GPUs (8–12 min to fully provision dedicated prewarmed nodes) and burst spots (3–5 min). Also watch for KV cache eviction during heavy churn.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: New preheat job started for acme-poc-warmup at 2401122800 by liz

sarah: Awesome. I'll collate these into the security QA answers and the pricing sheet. Need SOC2 docs from @julia and the KMS diagram for the security questionnaire.

julia: Will attach SOC2 + KMS guide in the ticket now. Note: customer asked about key-rotation cadence — we support 30/90/365 day rotation policies via KMS.

alex: Thanks — next steps: I'll confirm with Acme that 6k = requests/min (sarah confirmed on call), send runbook+quote, and schedule capacity provisioning for next Tue if they sign. If anything else pops up re: license or compliance constraints ping in this thread. :thumbsup:
